pr_title: crypto/sleep.c: Have the fallback ossl_sleep_secs() sleep all the seconds
pr_body:
In the internal `ossl_sleep_secs()`, we have a lot of machination to ensure
that we compensate for the fact that `sleep()` takes an `unsigned int`, not a
`uint64_t`, by sleeping the appropriate amount of chunks of seconds that can't
fit in an `unsigned int`.  We did forget to sleep the remaining seconds (the
remaining amount that does fit in an `unsigned int`), though, which means that
a simple call like `OSSL_sleep(2000)` wouldn't sleep at all.

Fixes #20524
pr_comments:
I marked this urgent, 'cause VMS tests are currently failing (see the VMS builds in https://ci.buildbot.openssl.org).
I also marked it `test: exempted`, 'cause it can be argued that the CMP client test did indeed test `OSSL_sleep()`, albeit accidently rather than on purpose.  I would welcome a separate test for `OSSL_sleep()`, but would suggest that this can be done in a separate PR.

This should not be marked "urgent" as it should go through the normal review process.
Urgent is meant to be reserved for exceptional circumstances.
If this ends up  not considered urgent, I suggest adding the missing test for `OSSL_sleep()` right away in this PR.

> 2 billion seconds sleeping

Nit pick: 4 billion seconds :). i.e. 136 years (approximately) - I'm sure the system will have gone out of extended support (even for an LTS) by then!

(And the worrying about single seconds here or there would miss the many leap seconds that would occur in that time)

> This should not be marked "urgent" as it should go through the normal review process. Urgent is meant to be reserved for exceptional circumstances.

We've used it for build/test breaks on platforms we have CIs for.  Has that condition changed?

> Why do we need to have sleep that supports more than 2 billion seconds sleeping? Wouldn't it be better to just max it out at UINT_MAX sleep as that is essentially forever?
> 
> ```
> if (secs > UINT_MAX)
>      secs = UINT_MAX;
> sleep((unsigned int)secs);
> ```

This PR isn't intended for that sort of refactoring.

> > > 2 billion seconds sleeping
> > 
> > 
> > Nit pick: 4 billion seconds :). i.e. 136 years (approximately) - I'm sure the system will have gone out of extended support (even for an LTS) by then!
> 
> Right, and more importantly: no IT system will be up and running that long.
> 
> Still, for conceptual reasons, I'd favor the pretty straightforward and fully correct
> 
> ```
>     while (secs > UINT_MAX) {
>         sleep(UINT_MAX);
>         secs -= UINT_MAX;
>     }
>     sleep((unsigned int)secs);
> ```

I would argue that the `_WIN32` variant of `OSSL_sleep()` should be refactored the same way, then, as it's essentially the exact same function as `ossl_sleep_secs()`, apart from the platform sleeping function used and the type for the time to sleep.
Alternative in #20533. There is actually one reason why there should not be a loop.

So, am I to understand that the success of this test is about a timeout engaging, and that the VMS box is too slow (i.e. doesn't check the timeout status soon enough, or something like that)?

This test case expects a total (i.e., overall transaction) timeout. This should happend after 1 second, after the client has been requested to wait for 2 seconds before polling again. This is what usually (and also on your Linux box) happens.

On VMS, looks like the client did not really wait (though it should have waited for 2 seconds) but immediately polled again, which lead to an unexpected successful termination of the transaction within 1 second, so no timeout occurred.

I suspect `OSSL_sleep()` does not work correctly, called in `cmp_client.c`:
```
OSSL_sleep((unsigned long)(1000 * check_after));
```
I don't suspect `time()` has an issue such that the calculation in `cmp_client.c` of when the timeout is flagged goes wrong:
```
int64_t time_left = (int64_t)(ctx->end_time - exp - time(NULL));`
```

Would be good to have independent test cases for `OSSL_sleep()`, `time()`, and/or their interplay.
